messages:
vikram: quick thought — we should add runtime telemetry + automated fallbacks for low-bit execution paths. we've seen small but customer-visible regressions on some prompts with 4-bit. want a lightweight safety net rather than manual rollbacks.
adele: +1. we need to decide what signals actually trigger a fallback. quality delta? n-gram overlap? human eval failures? also cost/latency tradeoffs.
ryan: how do customers control this? per-request hint or model-level policy? exposing too many knobs = confusion.
olivia: recommend: default to "auto" (platform decides), allow model-pin and explicit per-request override. surface the fallback rate and recent regressions in Console. opt-in for lowbit for hosted customers.
paul: logging: keep diffs as hashes and small sketches to avoid storing user text. also record seed prompt IDs so we can repro offline.
ci-bot: canary run results: 2026-02-28 09:12 — 200 eval prompts, 12 triggered fallback on 4-bit fast path, median quality delta 0.8%, worst-case 4.3%. artifacts pushed to s3://redwood-ci/quant-canary/1832104321/
vikram: rough config idea — fallback policy as a small DSL so runtime can act without extra code:
```json
{
  "fallback_policy": {
    "trigger": "quality_delta",
    "threshold": 0.01,
    "window": 50,
    "actions": ["switch_to_int8","notify_on_console"],
    "cooldown_secs": 3600
  }
}
```
adele: love the cooldown idea. also suggest sampling fraction so we only recompute a subset to estimate true quality impact. re-running all requests would blow cost.
ryan: API surface proposal: add header or SDK param `precision_preference` enum = ["auto","high","low"]. auto uses profiles + heuristics, high pins to 8/16-bit, low allows 4-bit. default auto.
olivia: telemetry metrics to emit: `quality_loss_rate`, `fallback_rate`, `avg_tokens_recomputed`, `canary_failures`. tie alerts to `quality_loss_rate > X` for 24h.
paul: for Private deployments we must provide an opt-out and ensure no uploaded prompt data leaves customer network. design must include a local-only metrics mode.
vikram: next steps: i'll draft an RFC with: fallback DSL, telemetry schema, SDK change, Console UX for rollouts/canaries, and canary test harness. @adele @ryan can you enumerate the eval checks we want in the RFC (perplexity vs soft-EM vs embedding-distance)?
adele: i'll put together a short list (perplexity delta, embedding cosine drop, token-level surprise histogram, spot human evals).
ryan: i'll sketch SDK header + migration notes. keep default behavior conservative.
olivia: add a dashboard mock for Console showing fallback hotspots by model + route.
paul: add compliance checklist for Private infra.
vikram: cool — thanks all. i'll have a first-pass RFC tomorrow. :thumbsup:
